previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with metastatic ER+ breast cancer involving the liver and bones was admitted with severe chest pain worsened by breathing and movement. A CT angiogram revealed a sternal fracture with a small retrosternal hematoma, likely due to malignancy, and a small right pleural effusion. She was experiencing acute hypoxemic respiratory failure, managed with supplemental oxygen initially, and was weaned to room air. Pain was poorly controlled on home morphine, so her dose was increased to 30 mg every 8 hours with Dilaudid for breakthrough pain. This led to opioid-induced ileus, which was managed with magnesium citrate and a reduction in breakthrough opioid. A new T11 vertebral compression fracture was identified on follow-up imaging. Her pain regimen was optimized, and she was discharged home with an adjusted opioid schedule, a bowel regimen, and plans to resume Taxol chemotherapy the following week.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ year old female with history of ER+ invasive
carcinoma of left breast (recurrent, metastatic to bone/liver,
currently on RT and on Taxol) and gastroparesis who presented
with nausea, abdominal pain, and vomiting.

# Nausea, vomiting: Symptoms were likely from known 
gastroparesis, for which she has had several admissions in the 
past. In addition, she reported symptoms were consistent with 
gastroparesis. GI had last seen the patient in early ___ 
with only intermittent nausea, not requiring metoclopramide at 
that time. Given her complex GI history with multiple surgeries, 
initial concern for obstruction though AXR without acute 
findings. Also consideration of chemotherapy-related nausea or 
morphine-related nausea, though less likely as she had no prior 
issues. ECG for cardiac issues also without issue. Home 
omeprazole continued. Her nausea resolved with IV medications 
(prochlorperazine, ondansetron, and metoclopramide) and 
transitioned to PO for discharge. She had daily ECGs/tele to 
monitor for QT changes, all without issue.

# Metastatic Breast cancer: Her anastrozole was continued while 
inpatient. She also received her scheduled radiation therapy 
___.

# Constipation: She carries prior diagnosis of IBS. Her home 
bowel regimen was continued with daily BMs.

# Back pain ___ pathologic compression fractures: Patient has
chronic back pain and was noted to have a compression fractures
seen on CT scan on ___, previously cleared by ___ in the past to 
go
home. While inpatient, her home pain regimen was continued and 
she received scheduled radiation treatments ___ - ___.

# Hx of sternal fracture: Patient was noted to have sternal 
fracture over one month ago which had been managed with pain 
medications as above.

# Anxiety: continued home citalopram, held lorazepam for 
somnolence

# Hypothyroidism: continued home synthroid
